lede: Public-domain photographs and maps of Williston and its neighbours, each with its source. More plates follow with the modules.
credit: Photographs from the Seaboard Air Line Railway Shippers Guide (1914) after the page images of the Internet Archive; the Sanborn fire-insurance maps of Williston, January 1923, from the Library of Congress (public domain) via Wikimedia Commons; photograph of the Acme Phosphate pit from the Florida Geological Survey Collection, State Archives of Florida, Florida Memory (public domain).

plates.caption: “Solid trainload of cucumbers leaving Williston, Fla., via the S. A. L. Ry., destined to eastern markets.”
plates.source: Seaboard Air Line Railway, Shippers Guide 1914, p. 71; Internet Archive seaboardairliner1914seab.

plates.caption: A field, the harvest in hampers, and a packing place: the railroad's three photographs of the cucumber trade at Williston, published to attract settlers.
plates.source: Seaboard Air Line Railway, Shippers Guide 1914, p. 71; Internet Archive seaboardairliner1914seab.

plates.caption: Pit of the Acme Phosphate Company, five miles southwest of Morriston, photographed by Herman Gunter on 21 April 1920.
plates.source: State Archives of Florida, Florida Memory, image GE0629, Florida Geological Survey Collection; public domain.

plates.caption: The Sanborn fire-insurance map: every building with its material and use, the depots and the tracks.
plates.source: Sanborn Map Company, Williston, Levy County, Florida, January 1923, sheet 1; Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.

plates.caption: The second sheet of the Sanborn map of January 1923.
plates.source: Sanborn Map Company, Williston, Levy County, Florida, January 1923, sheet 2; Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
